reason: The winding drum needs its bearing bracket before it can wind the lifting cord on the crane.
expectation: The drum and bracket should attach to the crane frame.

effect: The drum and crank first form a hand winch; the crank turns the drum to wind in cord.
reaction: The automatic assembly was useful, and the explanation of the longer crank was interesting.
reason: The assembled winch now looks ready to attach to the crane.
expectation: The winch should attach to the crane frame.

effect: The winch is attached to the crane, ready for the lifting parts.
reason: The lifting cord and hook should connect the winch to a load through the crane’s pulley.
expectation: The cord should be fitted to the winch and routed over the pulley.

effect: The lifting line is fitted; the crane still needs a way to hold and safely test a load.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: The pawl should engage the ratchet to hold the raised load, with the lever allowing release.
expectation: The pawl and release lever should attach to the winch mechanism.

effect: The pawl can hold the rope, but the crane still needs protection against tipping.
reaction: The distinction between holding the rope and stabilizing the crane is useful.
reason: The rear ballast should help balance the crane before testing a load.
expectation: The ballast should attach to the rear of the crane to improve stability.

effect: The ballast cannot be used yet, so I will test the rigged crane first.
reaction: I was surprised the ballast was not available before the test.
reason: The padded test weight looks like the next way to check the lifting mechanism before using the basket.
expectation: The crane should lift the test weight and reveal whether it is stable.
